idiom_name: pthread worker pool over a mutex/condition-variable task queue
implementation_notes: ISO C has no thread pool, task queue or future: the master creates N pthreads with pthread_create, publishes subtasks on a queue guarded by pthread_mutex_t and signalled with pthread_cond_t, and each worker loops popping work until it sees a sentinel. pthread_join is the aggregation barrier - the master reads the per-task result slots after the join - and pthread_cond_wait must be called in a while loop because wakeups are not guaranteed to be for this worker. Where the toolchain ships an OpenMP runtime, #pragma omp parallel for (or omp tasks) removes the queue code entirely, at the cost of fixing the decomposition to the loop shape.
pitfalls: The condition wait must be a while loop and the predicate (head == tail) must be re-checked after every wakeup; an if leaves the worker popping an empty queue.
Task and result storage is manual: the work items must outlive the workers, and a result written by a worker is only visible to the master after pthread_join or a mutex-protected hand-off.
There is no work stealing and no pool reuse: one global queue is a contention point after the join, and a worker that dies without a sentinel leaves the master blocked in pthread_join forever.
